To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
supply chain leaders need to be prepared for a future pandemic.
the pandemic has had a significant impact on supply chains, and that supply chains must be reimagined to meet the needs of the future.

supply chain leaders should: (1) develop a comprehensive understanding of their current and future supply chain needs and capabilities, (2) identify and address gaps in their current supply chain, (3) develop a comprehensive plan to address gaps, and (4) implement the plan.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues: How will the COVID-19 crisis impact the supply chain?
how healthcare supply chains will evolve in a post-COVID 19 environment, with a particular focus on PPE.
the implications of COVID 19 for supply chain management.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the COVID-19 pandemic has exposed the fragility of supply chain management.
COVID-19 has created a global health and economic crisis, which has affected every country in the world.
the pandemic has exposed the vulnerability of supply chains in the healthcare sector.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
supply chain leaders need to be more proactive and less reactive to supply chain challenges and opportunities.
supply chains are a critical part of the healthcare system and must be resilient and agile enough to respond to future pandemics.
we are not yet ready for the next crisis, but we are getting there.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the healthcare supply chain is not a single supply chain but rather an ecosystem of interrelated supply chains.
the COVID 19 pandemic will continue to have significant implications on supply chain management for the foreseeable future.
the healthcare supply chain is not prepared for another crisis.
